\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter09.HypercontractiveMomentSharpness}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Even-moment noise parameter]
\lean{FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p256-b003}
\label{FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise}
\leanok
For each nonnegative integer $r$, define the even-moment noise parameter by
$\displaystyle \frac{1}{\sqrt{2r-1}}$, with the expression interpreted in the real
numbers.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Even-moment bound coefficient]
\lean{FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p257-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p262-b003
}
\label{FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound}
\leanok
For nonnegative integers $r$ and $j$, define $\displaystyle
B_{r,j}=\frac{(2r-1)^j\binom{r}{j}}{\binom{2r}{2j}}$, where the powers, binomial
coefficients, and quotient are interpreted in the real numbers.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of the sharp even-moment noise]
\lean{FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise_nonneg}
\label{FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $r$, the sharp even-moment noise is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Square of the sharp even-moment noise]
\lean{FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise_sq}
\label{FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise_sq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise}
\difficulty{4}
For every positive natural number $r$, the square of the sharp even-moment noise is
$1/(2r-1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[First sharp even-moment bound]
\lean{FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound_one}
\label{FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound}
\difficulty{5}
For every positive natural number $r$, the sharp even-moment bound at index $1$ equals
$1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[First even moment from the second moment]
\lean{FABL.first_evenMoment_condition_redundant}
\label{FABL.first_evenMoment_condition_redundant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound, FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound_one}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $P$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let
$X:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$, and let $r\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $r>0$. If the expectation of
$X^2$ under $P$ is $1$, then the expectation of $X^{2\cdot 1}$ under $P$ equals
$\frac{(2r-1)r}{\binom{2r}{2}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[First even-moment benchmark]
\lean{FABL.not_first_evenMoment_gt_sharp}
\label{FABL.not_first_evenMoment_gt_sharp}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.first_evenMoment_condition_redundant, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $\mu$ be a
probability distribution on $\Omega$. Suppose $r$ is a positive integer and the
expectation of $X^2$ under $\mu$ is $1$. Then the expectation of $X^2$ cannot exceed the
first even-moment benchmark $(2r-1)r/\binom{2r}{2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp even coefficient identity]
\lean{FABL.sharp_even_coefficient_mul_bound}
\label{FABL.sharp_even_coefficient_mul_bound}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound, FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise, FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise_sq}
\difficulty{5}
Let $r$ and $l$ be natural numbers with $0<r$ and $l\le r$. Write $\eta_r=1/\sqrt{2r-1}$
and $B_{r,l}=(2r-1)^l\binom{r}{l}/\binom{2r}{2l}$. Then
$\binom{2r}{2l}\eta_r^{2l}B_{r,l}=\binom{r}{l}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Even moment coefficient gap]
\lean{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap}
\label{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\mathrm{law}$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, let $X\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $r,l\in\mathbb N$. Write $q_r$ for
the sharp even-moment noise quantity at $r$. The even moment coefficient gap is
$\binom{2r}{2l}q_r^{2l}\,\mathbb E_{x\sim\mathrm{law}}[X(x)^{2l}]-\binom rl$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing gap at the sharp moment bound]
\lean{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap_eq_zero_of_sharp}
\label{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap_eq_zero_of_sharp}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound, FABL.sharp_even_coefficient_mul_bound}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $P$ be a probability law on $\Omega$, let
$X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $r,l$ be nonnegative integers with $r>0$ and $l\le r$.
If $\mathbb E_P[X^{2l}]=(2r-1)^l\binom rl/\binom{2r}{2l}$, then
$\binom{2r}{2l}(2r-1)^{-l}\mathbb E_P[X^{2l}]-\binom rl=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Moment gap and sharp moment bound]
\lean{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap_le_zero_iff}
\label{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap_le_zero_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound, FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise, FABL.sharp_even_coefficient_mul_bound}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $P$ be a probability law on $\Omega$, let
$X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $r,l$ be nonnegative integers with $r>0$ and $l\le r$.
Then $\binom{2r}{2l}(2r-1)^{-l}\mathbb E_P[X^{2l}]-\binom rl\le0$ if and only if
$\mathbb E_P[X^{2l}]\le(2r-1)^l\binom rl/\binom{2r}{2l}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine even-moment coefficient expansion]
\lean{FABL.affine_evenMoment_sub_eq_coefficientGap_sum}
\label{FABL.affine_evenMoment_sub_eq_coefficientGap_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_affine_evenMoment_of_oddMoments, FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\mu$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let
$X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $r\in\mathbb N$. Suppose that $\mathbb
E_\mu[X^{2l-1}]=0$ for every integer $l$ with $1\le l\le r$, and let $t\in\mathbb R$.
Then
\[
\mathbb E_\mu\!\left[(1+\sigma_r tX)^{2r}\right]-(1+t^2)^r
=\sum_{l=0}^{r}\Delta_{r,l}(\mu,X)t^{2l},
\]
where $\sigma_r=1/\sqrt{2r-1}$ and
$\Delta_{r,l}(\mu,X)=\binom{2r}{2l}\sigma_r^{2l}\mathbb E_\mu[X^{2l}]-\binom rl$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Higher even-moment coefficient tail]
\lean{FABL.higherEvenMomentCoefficientTail}
\label{FABL.higherEvenMomentCoefficientTail}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\mu$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let
$X\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$, let $r,j\in\mathbb N$, and let $t\in\mathbb R$. If $g_l$
denotes the even-moment coefficient gap for $\mu$, $X$, $r$, and $l$, the higher
even-moment coefficient tail is $\sum_{l=0}^{r} -g_l t^{2l-2j}$ over indices with $j<l$,
with a zero summand for all other indices.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing higher-moment coefficient tail]
\lean{FABL.higherEvenMomentCoefficientTail_tendsto_zero}
\label{FABL.higherEvenMomentCoefficientTail_tendsto_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap, FABL.higherEvenMomentCoefficientTail}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\mathrm{law}$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $r,j$ be natural numbers. The higher
even-moment coefficient tail evaluated at $t=1/(m+1)$ tends to $0$ as the natural number
$m$ tends to infinity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Even-moment coefficient sum decomposition]
\lean{FABL.coefficientGap_mul_pow_add_higher}
\label{FABL.coefficientGap_mul_pow_add_higher}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $P$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. For nonnegative integers $r,l$, define
$G_l=\binom{2r}{2l}\bigl(1/\sqrt{2r-1}\bigr)^{2l}\mathbb E_P[X^{2l}]-\binom{r}{l}$. If
$j\le r$ and $G_l=0$ for every nonnegative integer $l<j$, then for every $t\in\mathbb
R$, $\sum_{l=0}^{r}G_l t^{2l}=G_jt^{2j}+\sum_{j<l\le r}G_l t^{2l}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Higher coefficient sum and tail identity]
\lean{FABL.higher_sum_eq_neg_pow_mul_tail}
\label{FABL.higher_sum_eq_neg_pow_mul_tail}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.evenMomentCoefficientGap, FABL.higherEvenMomentCoefficientTail}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\mathrm{law}$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, let $r,j$ be natural numbers, and let $t\in\mathbb
R$. The sum of the even-moment coefficient gaps times $t^{2l}$ over integers $l$ with
$j<l\le r$ equals $-t^{2j}$ times the higher even-moment coefficient tail at $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine test from an excessive even moment]
\lean{FABL.exists_affine_test_of_evenMoment_gt_sharp}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p257-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p258-b001
}
\label{FABL.exists_affine_test_of_evenMoment_gt_sharp}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.exists_positive_affine_test_of_evenMoment_gt_sharp, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfLpNorm, FABL.sharpEvenMomentBound, FABL.sharpEvenMomentNoise}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\mathrm{law}$ be a probability mass function
on $\Omega$, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $r,j$ be integers with $0<r$, $1\le j$,
and $j\le r$. Suppose the second moment of $X$ under $\mathrm{law}$ is $1$; every odd
moment of order $2l-1$ is zero for $1\le l\le r$; and for every integer $l$ with $1\le
l<j$, the even moment of order $2l$ equals $(2r-1)^l\binom{r}{l}/\binom{2r}{2l}$. If the
even moment of order $2j$ is strictly greater than
$(2r-1)^j\binom{r}{j}/\binom{2r}{2j}$, then there are real numbers $a,b$ such that the
$2r$-norm under $\mathrm{law}$ of $x\mapsto a+bX(x)/\sqrt{2r-1}$ is strictly greater
than the $2$-norm under $\mathrm{law}$ of $x\mapsto a+bX(x)$.
\end{theorem}
